title: voice-threads-raw-to-actionable-translation-brief-2028-02-17
content:
Purpose:
Convert a set of recent raw customer threads (support transcripts, CSM notes, product demos) into a compact list of actionable feature asks, quick-patch ideas, and decision hooks for product/eng to evaluate. This doc intentionally keeps the tone informal — consider it a working translation: raw voice -> ask-bones -> proposed next step.

Context and sampling: 
- Sources: 12 support threads (Feb 2028), 4 CSM demo notes, 3 partner workshop recordings.
- Customers sampled: 2 AI-native startups, 4 mid-market SaaS, 2 regulated financial orgs.
- Primary areas: latency/cost tradeoffs, private deployment observability, model-fallback behavior, prompt caching and deterministic reruns.

Raw voice excerpts (verbatim-ish snippets pulled from threads):
- "We hit a tail latency spike every afternoon — not sure if it's batching or our request pattern."
- "When the model downgrades, we lose structured tokens and the downstream parser fails. Need better graceful degradation."
- "Embedding costs are ballooning; can we cache per-customer embeddings or only update on schema change?"
- "Want local metrics in my VPC console — not just in Redwood Console. We need exportable traces."
- "We run critical flows in air-gapped infra. The onboarding doc is missing an example for HSM key rotation."

Synthesis: Themes and consolidated asks (ask-bones):
1) Tail-latency root-cause visibility (high frequency)
   - Ask: Provide per-route tail latency decomposition (batching delays, queue wait, kernel execution) at 99th/99.9th percentiles.
   - Why: Customers see infra-induced spikes and can’t tell if problem is their traffic or runtime scheduling.
   - Quick patch idea: Add an optional per-request trace id that surfaces breakpoint timestamps in Console (queue enter/exit, batch start/end, kernel start/end).
   - Owner suggestion: eng-observability + SRE; estimated 2 sprint spike (POC).

2) Deterministic graceful-degradation mapping (medium frequency, high impact for regulated customers)
   - Ask: When a fallback model is used, include a structured difference payload and a compatibility flag that indicates removed fields or changed tokenization so downstream parsers can branch safely.
   - Why: Downstream parsing fails silently when schema changes after fallback; causes production incidents.
   - Proposed product hook: model-variant metadata and a compact regression diff in API response when fallback occurs.
   - Risk: Extra response size; privacy considerations for diff payloads.

3) Per-customer embedding delta-cache policy (growing ask across customers using embeddings heavily)
   - Ask: Offer a configurable TTL and delta-update mode for embeddings: full, partial (schema-change only), and manual invalidation.
   - Why: Customers pay for repeated embedding calls for mostly-static docs; want cost reduction without added complexity.
   - Quick-win: Add a server-side option for "cache-per-customer with schema-check" that defaults to conservative TTL; surfaced via API header.

4) Private-deploy console export and trace collector (lower frequency but enterprise-critical)
   - Ask: VPC/private installs need a lightweight trace export endpoint (OTLP compatible) and a small console export pack (jsonl) for offline analysis.
   - Why: Security teams require auditable logs inside the customer boundary.
   - Suggestion: Provide a downloadable support bundle from private control plane UI; include configurable retention.

5) HSM/KMS onboarding examples and rotation checklist (urgent for on-prem customers)
   - Ask: Add a step-by-step HSM rotation appendix with exact CLI commands, common error messages, and troubleshooting tips.
   - Why: On-prem deployments stall during scheduled rotations.
   - Owner: private-deployments doc sprint; single-document addition + one recorded walkthrough.

Prioritization notes (quick RICE-ish heuristics):
- Tail-latency visibility: Reach=high, Impact=high (reduces incidents), Confidence=medium, Effort=medium -> Recommend: High priority (sprint allocation 2).
- Deterministic fallback payload: Reach=medium, Impact=high (prevents parser regressions), Confidence=medium, Effort=high -> Recommend: Medium-high (spec + API contract work).
- Embedding delta-cache: Reach=medium, Impact=medium-high (saves cost for frequent users), Confidence=high, Effort=low-medium -> Recommend: Quick win (small API flag + doc).
- Private trace export: Reach=low (enterprise-only), Impact=medium, Confidence=high, Effort=low -> Recommend: Quick feature for Private roadmap.
- HSM rotation docs: Reach=low, Impact=high for affected customers, Confidence=high, Effort=low -> Recommend: Immediate docs + support-runbook.

Open questions and trade-offs captured from threads: 
- How much extra response payload is acceptable for regression diffs during fallback? (privacy & bandwidth).
- Should embedding cache policy be opt-in per-customer or default with opt-out? (affects billing behavior).
- Do we allow customers to opt-in to per-request tracing in hosted API (PaaS) or restrict to Dedicated/Private due to cost/telemetry footprint?

Suggested next steps (practical & timeboxed):
1) Engineering spike (1 week): Proof-of-concept trace headers and a tiny Console panel that reads them. Owner: eng-observability. Deliverable: short demo + sample traces from a customer test harness.
2) Product & API spec (2 weeks): Define fallback-diff contract and privacy knobs. Owner: product-hosted-api + legal consult. Deliverable: API doc PR and example responses.
3) Docs sprint (3 days): HSM rotation appendix + recorded walkthrough. Owner: private-deployments docs. Deliverable: new page + internal playbook.
4) Pilot embedding delta-cache (2 sprints): Implement TTL and schema-check mode for 3 high-volume customers. Owner: eng-serving-runtime + solutions. Deliverable: telemetry showing token/cost savings.

Quick communication plan: 
- Ping ENG-OBS and SRE in sync channel with summary and ask for a 30-min alignment demo (aim this week).
- Share this note with CSMs for validation: ask 3 customers if they’ll pilot embedding delta-cache.

Appendix: Short customer vignettes (who said what and why it matters)
- FinReg corp: "When fallback happened we missed regulatory fields — audit showed gaps." -> This maps to deterministic fallback payload.
- Multi-doc SaaS: "Embedding costs double when nightly reindex runs — we just need delta updates." -> Embedding delta-cache.
- Start-up adtech: "Tail latencies are killing our conversion experiments — we can’t A/B reliably." -> Tail-latency visibility.

Notes-to-self: Keep this doc alive; convert to PRD if ENG-OBS spike validates feasibility. Check with legal on diff payload retention. Catalog pilot customers names in the secure CS tracker (not here).

-- end of brief --
